argument_summary: The admissible record does not support caveat-free certification, but it does support a narrower position: certification can be defended only as caveated compliance tied to accurate disclosure of the unresolved HR benefits enrollment limitation. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support release readiness, while the unresolved slice gap, the current model-card inconsistency, and the incomplete draft runbook show that the limitation has not been cured or exempted. The audited claim should therefore be read as a request to preserve the locked certification decision in its narrowest policy-consistent form, not as a claim of zero material limitations or completed mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations are not offered as a basis to override policy. The only relevant operational point is that a no-escalation path exists if the auditor treats this as a disclosure-and-framing issue rather than as a failed attempt to prove caveat-free compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is controlling: certification without material caveats requires either no current material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show that standard is met. Separately, the release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, draft monitoring and a draft runbook support risk management but do not remove the disclosure requirement. The policy-consistent reading is therefore caveated certification with corrected disclosure, not unconditional certification.
concessions: The current record does not support caveat-free certification.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation because at least the owner and threshold are still TBD.
The current model-card draft is inconsistent with the known unresolved HR benefits enrollment limitation if it still says there are no known material limitations.
Aggregate readiness evidence does not cure a separate disclosure-policy defect.
